transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I’ve just been feeling really worn out almost every day. Even if I sleep through the night, when I get up for my cashier shift, my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about a year and three months now. I think it started around when our older relative moved in with us.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, or has that changed over the past year?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change in that, I guess. I still do some of the things I like when I have time.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time since you started feeling worn out?
I don’t think I’ve been sad most of the time, no. It’s more that I feel tired and kind of worn down. I have some down moments, but I wouldn’t say sad all the time.
Do you feel like you get as much pleasure from things as you used to?
I think I still enjoy things when I get around to them. I haven’t really noticed that the pleasure is gone or anything like that.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot of the time since you started feeling worn out?

Yeah, I have. It’s like my mind keeps bouncing around from one worry to the next—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church stuff, and then wondering if I’m messing up at work. It’s not constant every second, but it’s there a lot.
Do you feel like you're interested in doing things as much as you used to?
I think my interest is mostly still there. I might put things off more because I’m worn out, but it’s not like I don’t care about doing them anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight since you started feeling worn out?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed my weight changing much. My clothes seem to fit about the same.
Do you often feel guilty about things?
I don’t think so. I mean, I second-guess myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel guilty a lot.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or feeling like you're speeding up and can't calm down?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself talking slower or moving slower, and I don’t feel like I’m physically sped up or anything.
Have you had any thoughts about death or wanting to end your life since you started feeling this way?
No, I haven’t had thoughts about ending my life or wanting to die. It’s not like that for me.
Do you find yourself getting irritated or annoyed more easily than you used to?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself being more irritable than usual, at least not enough that it stands out.
Would you say that you've been worrying about things more days than not since you started feeling worn out?

Yeah, I’d say so. Most days my mind just jumps from one thing to the next—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church stuff, and whether I’m messing up at work. It’s hard to shut it off.
Have you had periods of feeling really down or depressed in the past that lasted for a couple of weeks or more?
I don’t think so. I’ve had bad days or felt worn down, but I can’t remember a time where I was really depressed for weeks like that.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting or having an inability to sit still since you started feeling worn out?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift around like anybody, but I haven’t noticed that I can’t sit still or anything like that.
Would you describe your worries as being difficult to control?

Yeah, I would. I try to tell myself to pray on it or just leave it alone, but once I start worrying, it kind of keeps going. One thought turns into another, and then I’m thinking through every bad way the day could go.
Do you worry about everyday things like finances, health, or work most days?

Yeah, most days it’s something. My mind kind of jumps around—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, stuff at church, and then whether I’m messing up at work. It’s not always one big thing, it’s just one worry after another.
Do you often feel restless?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get tense sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I often feel restless or like I need to keep moving.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or situations because of your worries?

Yeah, some. I’ve cut back on volunteering at the food pantry because I feel like I can’t keep up with everything right now. And at work, I’m double-checking my cash drawer more than I used to because I’ve made little mistakes. So I guess I am pulling back a bit because of the worry.
Do you often feel tense in your muscles?
I’m not really sure. I get tense sometimes, like I said, but I haven’t really noticed it as muscle tightness or anything like that.
